findings.description: The user_data script contains plaintext AWS access key and secret key, which are stored in Terraform state and instance metadata in cleartext. Anyone with access to the instance metadata, console output, or Terraform state can retrieve these credentials.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data at rest on this volume is stored unencrypted and could be exposed if the underlying storage is compromised or snapshots are shared.
This snapshot is created from an unencrypted volume and has no encryption configured, so the snapshot data (and any copies/shares of it) remains unencrypted and exposed to unauthorized access.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance to brute-force and unauthorized access attempts from anywhere on the internet.

The security group also allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0 with unrestricted egress to all destinations, broadening the attack surface beyond what is likely necessary and enabling unrestricted outbound data exfiltration if the instance is compromised.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to direct internet access.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to direct internet access.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket used for VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, risking exposure of sensitive network traffic logs.
